name: Cindergrove
description: Spring elves are gifted a seed when young to carry for their whole lives. When it dies, the seed is planted here to become one of the trees of Cindergrove. The trees sprouted in this manner carry the essence of the elf, allowing its memories to endure and offering guidance to others. This grove is beautiful, with colorful flowers and butterflies contrasting with the grey-bark trees that give the place its name. A significant part of it was destroyed by orc raiders long ago, leaving part of the location barren as some ancient stone obelisks carved with druidic magic were damaged as the orcs pilled their emerald cores. To this day, the elves search for these stones, as each obelisk recovered means another section of Cindergrove that will be able to grow again. The elves value this location not only for its natural importance but also because of the memories it stores. Touching one of the trees can allow one to talk with the essence of an ancient elf, who can even impart memories to the living. Some of them have unfinished business and may ask for help; others have long goals and still try to convince others to take their mantle. Their rewards are intriguing; they impart knowledge into the person’s mind for a time, often between one day and a few weeks. However, rumors say that some powerful deceased elves can grant much more durable, or even permanent, powers. Many elves have even been trained by these essences as their masters, touching the trees every day to commune with them and receive wisdom for their daily practices, emerging as powerful heroes after long seclusion. Elven Essence Boon. The elven essence can grant specific memories, proficiency with a tool, language, skills, or even one or more class features from that elf’s past (of GM choice). Still, the memory or knowledge disappears entirely after a set amount of time. It is said that the elves visit Cindergrove when they know of an invasion to gain extraordinary abilities to defend their forest, which is one of the secrets of why they were never overtaken.
